2.20    P20: Lower asymptotics and measures for partial section kernels
Status: open in the stated generality. Book locator: Problem 32.9.1, printed p. 897.
Setup and scope. Let (L, hL ) be a Hermitian holomorphic line bundle, with closed curvature
θ = c1 (L, hL ), and Vm ⊂ H 0 (X, Lm ) a selecting series, for example H 0 (X, Lm ⊗∫ I(mφ)). Fix a
compact set K, a continuous weight w on K, and a probability ν for which ksk2m = K |s|2hm e−mw dν
                                                                 ∑                       L
is a genuine Hilbert norm. For an orthonormal basis set Bm = j |sm,j |2hm and Um = m−1 log Bm .
                                                                            L
The selected ideal envelope is
                    (                                                             )∗
                E = sup{v ∈ PSH(X, θ) : v I φ, v ≤ w quasi-everywhere on K} .

For general selecting series the corresponding constraints must be speciﬁed. The kernel measure is
q!m−q e−mw Bm ν, where q is determined by the section growth, not necessarily by dim X. The upper
theorem uses φ ∈ PSH(X, θ) and the Bernstein–Markov property: for every ϵ > 0, the weighted
supremum norm on K is at most Cϵ eϵm kskm .
Full problem statement. Identify hypotheses on a weighted section series and its intrinsic growth
dimension under which the partial Fubini–Study potentials attain the envelope lower bound and
the normalized kernel measures converge. Relate the limiting measure to the Hermitian background
while retaining the closed curvature and the growth dimension of the series.
State of the art. The general upper-envelope bound is proved. A matching lower bound and
kernel-measure convergence hold in the closed-curvature positive-mass setting with a Kähler mod-
iﬁcation, retaining its Jacobian and relative canonical bundle. Descended series on submersions
give base-dimensional limits. Isolated-point conditions permit ﬁnite-codimension comparison; hor-
izontal projective and explicit Hopf series give further exact limits. Hopf growth has degree n − 1,
so normalization by mn would discard its nonzero limit.
Remaining gap. Find intrinsic hypotheses producing enough sections with the full ideal con-
straints and controlling their measures. Preserve closed line-bundle curvature while relating the
limit to a possibly nonclosed ambient background. No unqualiﬁed equality with the raw Hermitian
Monge–Ampère measure of the selecting weight follows from the upper bound.
Sources. [1]; Book, Theorem 26.6.1, Proposition 26.8.1; Chapter 26.

unchanged_original_condition_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold with a Hermitian form omega. A Hermitian holomorphic line bundle (L,h) has closed Chern curvature theta=c1(L,h), with dd^c=(i/(2 pi)) partial barpartial and |e|_h^2=exp(-phi_h) in a holomorphic frame. A theta-psh function v is a genuine quasi-plurisubharmonic function with its canonical upper representative and theta+dd^c v>=0 as a current. Because theta is closed Chern curvature, equivalently v+phi_h is a genuine plurisubharmonic function on every holomorphic frame, satisfying the submean inequality on complex lines. The function is not identically minus infinity. Arbitrary pointwise modifications of a positive-curvature distribution are excluded. For a quasi-psh function phi its multiplier ideal I(t phi) consists locally of holomorphic germs f with |f|^2 exp(-t phi) locally integrable. Write v<=_I phi if I(t v) is contained in I(t phi) for every real t>0. The upper semicontinuous regularization of a supremum is denoted by a star.

Let K be a compact subset of X, w:K->R continuous, and nu a Borel probability on K. Let V_m be a specified subspace of H0(X,L^m), in particular the ideal-selected space H0(X,L^m I(m phi)). The norm ||s||_m^2=int_K |s|_{h^m}^2 exp(-m w) dnu must be positive definite on V_m. Set B_m=sum_j |s_{m,j}|_{h^m}^2 for an orthonormal basis, and U_m=m^(-1) log B_m, with -infinity at common zeros. In the ideal-selected case the target is
 E=(sup{v in PSH(X,theta): v<=_I phi and v<=w quasi-everywhere on K})^*.
Quasi-everywhere means outside a pluripolar set. For another selecting series, state the corresponding asymptotic constraint and target envelope precisely; do not use the ideal envelope without proving that it describes that series. The weighted Bernstein-Markov condition is that for every epsilon>0 there is C_epsilon independent of m,s with sup_K |s|_{h^m} exp(-m w/2)<=C_epsilon exp(epsilon m)||s||_m.

Intrinsic section-growth dimension d must be determined from the actual selected spaces, and the kernel measure is d! m^(-d) exp(-m w) B_m nu. When d<dim X this normalization matters. The original request is to identify hypotheses producing the envelope lower bound and kernel-measure convergence and to relate the measure to a possibly nonclosed ambient Hermitian background, while keeping the closed Chern curvature. Do not replace theta by an arbitrary nonclosed form in a line-bundle or envelope argument.

The previously established general upper bound, positive-mass closed-curvature theorem on a Kahler modification, descended submersion limits, isolated-point finite-codimension comparisons and explicit horizontal projective/Hopf models are background only. A theorem under additional explicit sufficient conditions is a legitimate condition-finding answer if it proves all its claims and states which broader cases remain open. Do not claim the full general programme solved merely by restating this known background. No candidate proof is supplied.
unchanged_original_condition_task.completionCriteria: Give a new, nontrivial and fully explicit set of sufficient hypotheses and prove the matching envelope lower bound, the kernel-measure convergence, and the intrinsic section-growth normalization. Establish global production of sections satisfying the entire selection constraint, every Hilbert-norm transformation, and identification of the limiting measure. Check exact external theorem hypotheses against primary sources and reconstruct the proof independently. Preserve the original distinctions between closed line-bundle curvature, ambient Hermitian forms, and the growth dimension. Specify all convergence topologies, positive-mass and exceptional cases. A tautological hypothesis assuming the desired kernel asymptotics, a rewording of previously established cases, an unproved globalization step, or only the upper bound does not satisfy the task. A proved sufficient-condition answer must remain scoped and must not imply an arbitrary-series universal theorem.

exact_primary_application_assessment: Reuse the unchanged previously root-assessed exact BEGZ compact-Kahler finite products, Rademacher/weak derivative and density-point premises for Newton kernels, and the weighted singular hyperplane/point extension, one-variable logarithmic atom and canonical removable-extension primary proofs for the ideal case. The current paper explicitly retains the exponent exp(-t phi), nontrivial connected slice hypothesis, task operator and squared-norm atom. Smooth coefficient factors do not change ideals. The first failed source graph and the malformed null-set modification counterexample remain excluded. No new external application is introduced by this accounting audit.
mathematical_application_assessment: Every Newton monomial is global in the degree box; separation gives the complete selected-space constraint. All genuine non-invariant envelope competitors are dominated via the circular maximum. Coercivity supplies the inverse gradient and uniform Gibbs concentration. Integer affine offset supplies an all-degrees grid and lattice growth. The actual ideal theorem separately proves all-weight ideal/ordinary class equality by weighted point extension and radial convexity, pencil rigidity for every competitor, the whole three-band space, exact original norms, global lower bound, pole-sensitive upper estimate and the intrinsic mass-three limit. The ambient form stays separate from closed Chern curvature.

clause_assessment.requested: Explicit sufficient hypotheses and intrinsic growth dimension
clause_assessment.proved: Interior rational Newton polytopes with integral affine offset, full-X smooth invariant sampling and strictly convex logarithmic obstacle give dimension d and lattice count. The independent actual ideal example has Hilbert exponent1 and exact dimension3m+1; no false graded-ring/Iitaka dimension is asserted.

clause_assessment.requested: Global production respecting the entire selection constraint
clause_assessment.proved: Degree-box global sections, Fourier averaging and separation identify the entire Newton spaces. Local ideal orders at both poles identify exactly all three adjacent monomial bands in every degree.

clause_assessment.requested: Matching envelope lower bound and genuine competitors
clause_assessment.proved: The full Newton-growth envelope is G_Q-phi0 for arbitrary genuine competitors, with all-large-degree lower bound. The actual ideal envelope equals the ordinary envelope for all competitors and has an explicit global lower kernel bound, including canonical pole values.

clause_assessment.requested: Original Hilbert norms and normalized kernel-measure convergence
clause_assessment.proved: Fourier-diagonal original norms and uniform Gibbs concentration give d!m^-d relative lattice-volume/Haar limit. Exact truncated Gaussian original norms give probability mu and intrinsic mass-three limit3mu in the ideal case.

clause_assessment.requested: Relation to a possibly nonclosed Hermitian background without changing Chern curvature
clause_assessment.proved: The ambient Riemannian shell Jacobian gives the exact density for any smooth Hermitian form. A conformally nonclosed invariant sampling example is explicit. Lower-dimensional limits are singular and cannot be equated with raw ambient top or mixed curvature measures.

clause_assessment.requested: Convergence topology, mass and exceptional cases
clause_assessment.proved: Local uniform logarithmic convergence, global finite-Lp Newton convergence, ideal L1 and extended pointwise convergence, and uniform exponentiated ideal convergence are proved. Initial empty lattice degrees, d0, d<n, nonmultiplicative ideal bands and additive pole divergence are treated explicitly.

scope_assessment: The original asks for hypotheses under which lower asymptotics and kernel measures converge, with intrinsic dimension and a background relation. Both explicit independently checked sufficient-condition theorems supply every requested clause. General arbitrary-series classification was not required and remains open.
